note: Help for moms outside the United States, built into world.html and countries/<slug>.html by scripts/ymt_build.py. Every listing needs a source it was checked against and the date. 'phone' is printed as the country writes it; 'dial' is the digits a phone in that country dials (or a full +country number for a line called from abroad). Never list a shelter address. Added November 19, 2026 at the owner's request: Yoga Mom Talk as a worldwide resource for moms.

worldwide.name: Find A Helpline
worldwide.what: A free directory of crisis and support lines in more than 130 countries. Pick your country and what you want to talk about, and it shows lines you can call, text or chat with.
worldwide.how: Choose your country on the site. Most lines are free and many are open any hour.

worldwide.name: Find your country's child helpline
worldwide.what: A list of the free child helplines in each country, run by the global network of child helplines. Parents and caregivers can call them about a child too.
worldwide.how: Open the list and choose your region, then your country.

worldwide.name: Postpartum Support International
worldwide.what: Help for depression, anxiety and other struggles during pregnancy and after a baby. It has more than 250 volunteer support coordinators around the world and free online support groups.
worldwide.how: Open the support map and choose your country to find a coordinator, a crisis line and groups near you.

worldwide.name: La Leche League breastfeeding support
worldwide.what: Free breastfeeding help from volunteer leaders who have nursed their own babies, in more than 80 countries. Meetings are free and children are welcome.
worldwide.how: Go to the website and find a leader or group in your country or language.

worldwide.name: International Social Service
worldwide.what: Help when a family is split across borders: custody and contact disputes between countries, family mediation and child protection. It works through partner offices in more than 120 countries.
worldwide.how: Contact the ISS office in your country through the global network's website.

worldwide.name: U.S. citizens abroad: emergency help
worldwide.what: For American moms living or traveling outside the U.S. The State Department helps U.S. citizens abroad with emergencies, including crime, arrest, lost passports and a parent taking a child across a border.
worldwide.how: Contact the nearest U.S. embassy, or call any hour. From the U.S. and Canada, call 1-888-407-4747.
worldwide.phone_label: From outside the U.S. and Canada, any hour

emergency.label: Police or an emergency ambulance. In Buenos Aires city and some nearby areas, 107 also sends an ambulance

resources.name: Línea 144
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day of the year, for anyone facing gender-based violence or at risk: physical, psychological, sexual, economic and more. A team of lawyers, psychologists and social workers listens and advises.
resources.how: Call 144, or send a WhatsApp to +54 9 11 2771-6463. Video calls are available for deaf people. In Spanish.

resources.name: National mental health line
resources.what: Free, confidential and open any hour, for a mental health crisis, thoughts of suicide or self-harm, or when you are worried about someone. Trained staff can send emergency help.
resources.how: Call 0800-999-0091. In Spanish.

resources.name: Línea 102
resources.what: A free, confidential line on children's and teenagers' rights, for when a child is being hurt or their rights are being ignored.
resources.how: Call 102. In Spanish.

resources.name: Asignación Universal por Hijo (AUH)
resources.what: A monthly payment for each child under 18 (with no age limit for a child with a disability), for parents who are out of work, in informal or domestic work, or on the monotributo social.
resources.how: Check your contact details and family links in mi ANSES; once they are confirmed, payments start. Keep your child's check-ups and vaccines up to date to get the full amount.

resources.name: Asignación por Embarazo
resources.what: A monthly payment during pregnancy, for up to 9 months, for women who are out of work, in informal or domestic work, or on the monotributo social.
resources.how: Sign up to the Programa Sumar, which confirms your pregnancy, and apply from week 12. The last 20% is paid after the birth once your Sumar check-ups are recorded.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: 1800RESPECT
resources.what: Australia's national counselling and support line for domestic, family and sexual violence. Free, confidential and open any hour, with free interpreters.
resources.how: Call, text 0458 737 732, or chat on the website. You can also call for someone you are worried about.

resources.name: Lifeline crisis support
resources.what: Free, confidential crisis support any hour for anyone in Australia who feels overwhelmed, is in emotional distress or is thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call, text 0477 13 11 14, or chat online. Through TIS on 131 450 you can ask for Lifeline in your language.

resources.name: PANDA perinatal mental health helpline
resources.what: Free counselling and support from a national helpline for new and expecting parents affected by anxiety, depression or postnatal psychosis, or finding it hard to become a parent.
resources.how: Call during opening hours (they are on PANDA's website). The helpline works in many languages.

resources.name: National Breastfeeding Helpline
resources.what: Free breastfeeding help any hour from trained volunteer counsellors, all mums who have breastfed. The line is funded by the Australian Government.
resources.how: Call 1800 mum 2 mum. For an interpreter, call TIS on 131 450 and ask them to call the helpline.

resources.name: Pregnancy, Birth and Baby
resources.what: A free information and support line for pregnancy, birth and the first years of parenting, funded by the Australian Government.
resources.how: Call, or use the video call option on the website.

resources.name: Family Tax Benefit
resources.what: A two-part payment that helps with the cost of raising children. Part B is for single parents, grandparent carers and some couples with one main income.
resources.how: Check who can get it on the Services Australia website, then claim online through myGov with Centrelink linked.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance. 911 works too

resources.name: The Bahamas Crisis Centre
resources.what: Help any hour for anyone facing domestic violence, sexual abuse or another crisis.
resources.how: Call 242-328-0922. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: PACE Bahamas
resources.what: Help for teen mothers to finish high school, and work to prevent teen pregnancy.
resources.how: Call 242-356-0943 or 242-676-5944. Normal call charges may apply.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance. Free, any hour

resources.name: National Helpline 109
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Children Affairs
resources.what: A free line, open any hour, for women and children facing violence. It can arrange rescue, legal and counselling help, health referrals, and help to stop a child marriage.
resources.how: Dial 109.

resources.name: Child Helpline 1098
resources.what: A free helpline for children, open every day and night, holidays included, in Bangla.
resources.how: Dial 1098 from anywhere in Bangladesh.

resources.name: Legal aid helpline 16699
resources.what: Free legal advice by phone for people who cannot afford a lawyer, and where to find your nearest legal aid office.
resources.how: Call 16699. It is toll-free. This number replaced the old 16430 in November 2025.

emergency.label: Police. Ambulance, 511. Fire, 311

resources.name: Lifeline Barbados
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's mental health hotline, open any hour. Operators trained in crisis support listen, help and refer you on.
resources.how: Call 536-4500. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Advocates Against Domestic Abuse (AADA) helpline
resources.what: A helpline open any hour for people facing abuse, with crisis support, counselling and advocacy.
resources.how: Call 246-432-2873. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Child Care Board
resources.what: The agency that runs child protection in Barbados, for children under 18. Contact it to report a child you are worried about. If a child is in danger right now, call 211.
resources.how: Call the office on 246-535-2800. Normal call charges may apply.

emergency.label: Military Police, when someone is in danger right now. For an ambulance (SAMU), call 192

resources.name: Ligue 180
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day, weekends and holidays too. It explains your rights, points you to specialist services near you and takes reports of violence against women.
resources.how: Call 180, or send a WhatsApp to (61) 9610-0180. In Portuguese, with Libras (sign language) for deaf women. If violence is happening now, call 190.

resources.name: CVV (Centro de Valorização da Vida)
resources.what: Volunteers offer emotional support and suicide prevention, in confidence and without judgment, any hour.
resources.how: Call 188. The call is free. You can also chat or write on the website. In Portuguese.

resources.name: SAMU 192
resources.what: Free emergency medical help and ambulances, any hour, every day.
resources.how: Call 192.

resources.name: Disque 100
resources.org: Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship
resources.what: Free, any hour, to report abuse or neglect of children and teenagers, and other human rights violations.
resources.how: Call 100 from any phone, or send a WhatsApp to (61) 99611-0100. In Portuguese.

resources.name: Prenatal care in the public health system (SUS)
resources.what: Regular pregnancy check-ups at your local public health unit, with care through the birth and a check-up afterwards.
resources.how: Go to the primary care unit nearest your home as soon as you think you are pregnant, ideally by week 12. Visits are monthly to week 28, every two weeks to week 36, then weekly.

resources.name: Bolsa Família
resources.org: Ministry of Development and Social Assistance (MDS)
resources.what: Monthly money for families with income up to R$218 per person, with extra for each child under 7, and for pregnant women, nursing mothers and children 7 to 18.
resources.how: Sign up in the Cadastro Único at your city's social assistance office. For information, call Disque Social 121.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.what: Call or text 9-8-8 any hour, anywhere in Canada, if you are thinking about suicide or are worried about someone. Free, in English and French.
resources.how: Call or text 988. If 988 does not work on your phone, call 1-833-456-4566.

resources.name: ShelterSafe: find a women's shelter
resources.what: A map of shelters and transition houses for women and children leaving violence. Click your area to get the nearest shelter's 24-hour crisis number.
resources.how: Open the map and choose your area. You do not have to stay at a shelter to get help such as safety planning.

resources.name: Kids Help Phone
resources.what: Free, confidential support any hour for children, teens and young adults across Canada, by phone, text or chat, in English and French.
resources.how: Your child can call, or text CONNECT to 686868. Interpreters are available in many languages.

resources.name: 211 Canada
resources.what: One free number for community and government help near you: food, housing, money, health and more. Open any hour, in more than 150 languages.
resources.how: Dial 2-1-1, or search 211.ca or the 211 app.

resources.name: Canada child benefit
resources.what: A tax-free monthly payment if you live with and care for a child under 18. The amount depends on family income and the number and ages of your children.
resources.how: Apply when your baby is born or a child comes to live with you. You can apply when you register the birth, online through My Account, or with form RC66.

emergency.label: Carabineros, the police. For an ambulance (SAMU), call 131

resources.name: Fono 1455
resources.org: Servicio Nacional de la Mujer y la Equidad de Género (SernamEG)
resources.what: A free national line for women who are facing, or have faced, gender-based violence, and for people who want to help them. It offers guidance and psychological and legal support.
resources.how: Call 1455, every day from 8am to midnight, holidays too, or send a WhatsApp to +56 9 9700 7000. In Spanish. For the police, call 133; Carabineros' family line is 149.

resources.name: Línea *4141
resources.what: Free, confidential help any hour for a crisis linked to suicide: thoughts of suicide, extreme emotional pain or wanting to hurt yourself. A psychologist answers.
resources.how: Dial *4141 from any mobile phone. In Spanish.

resources.name: SAMU 131
resources.what: The ambulance service for medical emergencies when a life is at risk.
resources.how: Call 131.

resources.name: Fono Infancia
resources.what: Free advice from psychologists who specialise in childhood, for parents and anyone caring for children.
resources.how: Call 800 200 818 or use the online chat, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 7pm. In Spanish.

resources.name: Chile Crece Más (formerly Chile Crece Contigo)
resources.what: Support for children and their families from the first prenatal check-up in the public health system, including a newborn kit for babies born in public hospitals and parenting programmes.
resources.how: Your public health centre and your municipality can tell you what is offered where you live. Being in the Registro Social de Hogares opens up more support.

resources.name: Subsidio Familiar (SUF)
resources.what: $22,007 a month for each child under 18, for families in the most vulnerable 60% of the Registro Social de Hogares who have no social security. Pregnant women can apply for the maternal subsidy from the fifth month.
resources.how: Apply at your municipality with your child's birth certificate, and their health check card (under 6) or school certificate (6 and over).

emergency.label: The national number for emergencies and safety

resources.name: Línea 155
resources.what: Free and confidential, any hour, every day, for women facing violence and anyone who knows of a case. It explains your rights, how to report, and where to get legal and health help.
resources.how: Call 155. In Spanish.

resources.name: Línea 106
resources.what: Free, confidential support from mental health professionals, any hour, for anyone in crisis, at risk, or who needs to talk.
resources.how: Call 106 from a landline or mobile. Video calls can be booked too. In Spanish.

resources.name: Línea 141
resources.what: A free national line, any hour, to protect children and teenagers: when a child is scared at home, being hurt, or going without food, school or health care.
resources.how: Call 141. ICBF's general line, 018000 91 80 80, is open weekdays from 8am to 5pm.

resources.name: Desarrollo Infantil en la Familia
resources.what: Support from pregnancy until age five: group meetings each week, at least one home visit a month, early learning and nutrition. Children under two, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers come first.
resources.how: Go to the ICBF zonal centre (Centro Zonal) nearest your home.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance through the national 9-1-1 system

resources.name: Línea Vida
resources.what: A free line, open any hour, to report violence and get guidance.
resources.how: Call 809-200-1202. In Spanish. In danger right now, call 911.

resources.name: Línea Mujer *212
resources.what: A free, confidential line for women facing gender-based or family violence, open any hour, every day.
resources.how: Dial *212 from any mobile phone (Altice, Claro or Viva). In Spanish.

resources.name: Cuida tu Salud Mental
resources.what: Trained behavioural health specialists listen and help you find care.
resources.how: Call 809-200-1400, every day from 8am to midnight. In Spanish. The government plans to move this line to 811 during 2026, so if this number does not answer, try 811.

emergency.label: Any emergency, free, any hour. Also 15 for medical help, 17 for police, 18 for fire

resources.name: 3919 Violences Femmes Info
resources.what: A free, anonymous national line for women facing any kind of violence, and for the people around them. Open any hour, every day. It listens, explains your options and points you to help near you.
resources.how: Call 3919. It does not show on the phone bill. Listening is in French and, at set times, 12 other languages including English, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese and Polish. It is not an emergency line: in danger right now, call 17.

resources.name: 3114, national suicide prevention line
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day. Nurses and psychologists answer if you are thinking about suicide, or if you are worried about someone.
resources.how: Call 3114 from anywhere in France. The line is in French.

resources.name: 119 Enfance en danger
resources.what: For children in danger and any adult worried about a child. Free, confidential and open any hour.
resources.how: Call 119. Young people under 18 can also chat online every day from 3pm to 8:30pm.

resources.name: 115 Samu social
resources.what: The number to call when you have nowhere to stay. Free from any phone in mainland France and overseas, any hour, every day.
resources.how: Call 115.

resources.name: PMI centres (Protection maternelle et infantile)
resources.what: Free health centres, open to all, for pregnant women and children up to age 6: pregnancy check-ups, care for you after the birth, baby check-ups, growth and development checks and vaccines.
resources.how: Find your nearest centre on your département's website or in the Service-public.fr directory.

resources.name: Prime à la naissance
resources.what: A one-off payment of €1,093.11 for each baby, for families under an income limit. It is paid in the seventh month of pregnancy.
resources.how: Declare your pregnancy first, then apply online with the Caf (or the MSA if you are in the farming scheme).

emergency.label: Ambulance and fire. For the police, call 110

resources.name: Hilfetelefon Gewalt gegen Frauen
resources.org: Federal Office for Family and Civil Society Tasks (BAFzA)
resources.what: A free, anonymous national line for women facing any kind of violence, open around the clock, every day of the year. Family, friends and professionals can call too.
resources.how: Call 116 016. Help is in German and 18 other languages with interpreters, in German Sign Language and in easy German. You can also get help online on the website.

resources.name: TelefonSeelsorge
resources.what: Someone to talk to, free and anonymous, day and night, whatever is weighing on you. You can also write by chat or email, or talk face to face at a local centre.
resources.how: Call 0800 111 0 111, 0800 111 0 222 or 116 123. The line is in German.

resources.name: Hilfetelefon Schwangere in Not
resources.what: Free, confidential help any hour for pregnant women who feel alone or in trouble, anonymous if you wish. It can also help you find a pregnancy counselling centre near you.
resources.how: Call 0800 40 40 020 from anywhere in Germany. Help is in 19 languages, including sign language. Chat and email are on its website.

resources.name: Elterntelefon
resources.what: A free, anonymous line for parents and other adults who are worried about a child or about family life.
resources.how: Call 0800 111 0 550: Monday, Wednesday and Friday 9am to 5pm, Tuesday and Thursday 9am to 7pm. In German. Children and teens can call 116 111 themselves, Monday to Saturday, 2pm to 8pm.

resources.name: Bundesstiftung Mutter und Kind
resources.what: Money for pregnant women in financial hardship, for things like maternity clothes, the baby's first things, the home and childcare. It is not taken off Bürgergeld or other benefits.
resources.how: Apply at a pregnancy counselling centre (Schwangerschaftsberatungsstelle) near you, before the baby is born. Counselling there is free and can be anonymous.

resources.name: Kindergeld (child benefit)
resources.what: €259 a month for each child from January 2026, whatever your income. It goes to the parent the child lives with.
resources.how: It is paid by the Familienkasse at the Agentur für Arbeit. Families on a low income can also get Kinderzuschlag, up to €297 a month per child on top, and can apply online with a BundID account.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance, on every mobile network

resources.name: Orange Support Centre
resources.org: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection
resources.what: A free line for anyone facing abuse at home or sexual violence. You can talk it through, get legal help and help finding emergency shelter, and learn about your health and rights.
resources.how: Call 0800 111 222. It is toll-free.

resources.name: National mental health helpline
resources.what: The national line for anyone who is struggling or having thoughts of suicide. It can link you to mental health care near where you live.
resources.how: Call 0800 678 678. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: DOVVSU helpline
resources.org: Ghana Police Service, Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit
resources.what: The police unit for domestic violence, child abuse and sexual violence. It is there for every victim, women, children and men.
resources.how: Call 055 100 0900. Normal call charges may apply. If you are in danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: Free health insurance in pregnancy
resources.what: Pregnant women can join the National Health Insurance Scheme without paying. Care in pregnancy under the scheme is free, including check-ups, lab tests, scans and emergency care.
resources.how: Register in person at your district NHIS office. Bring your antenatal card or a note from your doctor or midwife.

resources.name: LEAP cash transfer
resources.org: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection
resources.what: Cash paid every two months to the poorest households, including pregnant women and mothers with a baby under one. Families in LEAP also get free health insurance.
resources.how: Households are chosen by the LEAP Management Secretariat at the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: Women Helpline 181
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Child Development
resources.what: A free helpline for women facing violence or distress, open any hour. It links you to the police, a One Stop Centre, a hospital or legal help.
resources.how: Dial 181 from any phone.

resources.name: Sakhi One Stop Centres
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Child Development
resources.what: A centre in each district for women affected by violence, with medical help, legal help, police help, counselling and a short stay in a safe place, all under one roof.
resources.how: Call 181 and ask for your district's One Stop Centre, or find it on the Mission Shakti website.

resources.name: Tele-MANAS mental health helpline
resources.org: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
resources.what: Free mental health support by phone any hour, from the national tele-mental health programme, in many Indian languages.

resources.name: Child Helpline 1098
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Child Development
resources.what: A free emergency line for children who need care and protection, now linked with the national emergency number 112.
resources.how: Dial 1098 for a child in danger or distress.

resources.name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Child Development
resources.what: A maternity cash benefit paid to pregnant women and new mothers, ₹5,000 for the first living child, sent to her bank account.
resources.how: Apply at your Anganwadi centre or online on the PMMVY portal with your Aadhaar and bank details.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance (999 works too). Free from any phone

resources.name: Women's Aid National Freephone Helpline
resources.what: Free, confidential support any hour for women facing domestic abuse, including coercive control and stalking. It can refer you to refuges and local services, with interpreters in many languages.
resources.how: Call any time. If you cannot speak when you call, they will still listen.

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.what: Someone to talk to, free, any time of day or night, whatever you are going through. You do not have to be suicidal to call.
resources.how: Call 116 123 from any phone.

resources.name: askonefamily helpline
resources.what: Information and a listening ear for people parenting alone, sharing parenting or separating: welfare, money, family law, housing, childcare and parenting.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday, 10am to 3pm. If nobody is free, they take your details and call you back.

resources.name: Child Benefit
resources.what: A monthly payment of €140 for each child, whatever your income. For babies born from December 2024 a Newborn Baby Grant of €280 comes with the first payment.
resources.how: If your baby is born in Ireland, a claim starts when you register the birth. Otherwise use form CB1 or MyWelfare.ie within 12 months.

emergency.label: The European emergency number, free from any phone

resources.name: 1522 anti-violence and stalking line
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day, for anyone facing gender-based violence or stalking. Trained staff listen and point you to support services near you, and you can stay anonymous.
resources.how: Call 1522 from a landline or mobile. Help is in Italian, English, French, Spanish and Arabic.

resources.name: Telefono Amico Italia
resources.what: Volunteers listen if you feel alone, low or overwhelmed, or have thoughts of suicide.
resources.how: Call 02 2327 2327 every day from 9am to midnight, or send a WhatsApp to 324 011 7252. The service is free; you pay only your normal call cost. In Italian.

resources.name: Telefono Azzurro
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day, for children and teens up to 18, and for parents and other adults who want advice about a child.
resources.how: Call 19696 or use the web chat. In Italian.

resources.name: Assegno unico e universale
resources.what: A monthly payment for each child, from the seventh month of pregnancy up to age 21. The amount depends on your ISEE (family income and assets); families without an ISEE still get the minimum.
resources.how: Apply online at inps.it, through the INPS contact centre, or with free help from a patronato.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance or the fire service, dial 110

resources.name: Woman Inc. Crisis Centre Hotline
resources.what: A 24-hour hotline for women facing domestic violence, rape, incest or sexual harassment. Trained volunteers answer, and it can help a woman leaving an abusive partner find emergency shelter.
resources.how: Call any hour. Counselling in person is by appointment or walk-in on weekdays in Kingston and Montego Bay.

resources.name: Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Helpline (888-NEW-LIFE)
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's free helpline for anyone in Jamaica who is struggling, in crisis or thinking about suicide. Psychologists give first counselling and refer callers on for more help.
resources.how: Call 888-NEW-LIFE (888-639-5433). It is toll-free.

resources.name: 211 child abuse reporting line
resources.org: Child Protection and Family Services Agency
resources.what: A free 24-hour line for children, and for any adult worried that a child is being abused or neglected. Trained officers answer and pass the report to the right agency.
resources.how: Dial 211 from any phone. You can also send a WhatsApp or text to 876-878-2882.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance. 112 also works from a mobile

resources.name: National GBV Helpline 1195
resources.org: Healthcare Assistance Kenya, with the State Department for Gender
resources.what: Kenya's free national line for anyone facing sexual, physical, emotional or financial abuse at home. Counsellors answer any hour and connect callers to medical care, legal aid and safe places to stay.
resources.how: Dial 1195 from any phone. Family, friends or neighbours can call for someone else.

resources.name: Kenya Red Cross 1199
resources.what: A free 24-hour line run by the Kenya Red Cross. Its counsellors give emotional and psychosocial support to people in distress.
resources.how: Dial 1199. If it does not connect, call the Red Cross on +254 703 037 000.

resources.name: National Child Helpline 116
resources.org: Department of Children Services with Childline Kenya
resources.what: A free 24-hour line for children, and for adults worried about a child. It offers counselling and can arrange rescue, safe shelter, medical care and legal help.
resources.how: Dial 116, or send a WhatsApp to 0722 116 116.

emergency.label: Police, ambulance, fire and civil defence. Free, even with no credit

resources.name: Talian Kasih 15999
resources.what: A line open any hour for women, children and families in crisis, including abuse, neglect and sexual harassment. It offers counselling, protection and welfare help.
resources.how: Dial 15999, or send a WhatsApp to 019-261 5999. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Befrienders Kuala Lumpur
resources.what: Free, confidential emotional support any hour of the day, for anyone who is struggling or thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call 03-7627 2929. The support is free; normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Women's Aid Organisation (WAO)
resources.what: Help for women facing domestic violence, including crisis support and a safe shelter.
resources.how: Call the WAO Hotline on 03-3000 8858, 9am to 5pm, or text or WhatsApp TINA on 018-988 8058 any hour. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Children's Financial Aid (BKK)
resources.what: Monthly help for families caring for children: RM250 for each child aged 6 or under and RM200 for each child aged 7 to 18, up to RM1,000 a family.
resources.how: Apply online on eBantuan JKM, or in person at your district Social Welfare Office.

emergency.label: Police, fire and medical emergencies across the country

resources.name: Línea de la Vida
resources.org: Comisión Nacional de Salud Mental y Adicciones (CONASAMA)
resources.what: Mexico's free national line for emotional support, run by the health ministry. Trained professionals answer any hour about crisis, thoughts of suicide, violence, and alcohol or drug use.
resources.how: Call 800 911 2000 from any phone in Mexico. The line is in Spanish.

resources.name: Red Nacional de Refugios helpline
resources.what: A national network of shelters for women and their children escaping violence. Its helpline gives support and can help find a safe place to stay anywhere in Mexico.
resources.how: Call 800 822 4460. Shelter addresses are kept private for safety.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: Veilig Thuis
resources.what: The national advice and reporting centre for domestic violence and child abuse, whether it is happening to you or someone else. Free and open any hour.
resources.how: Call 0800-2000. You can also chat anonymously on weekdays from 9am to 5pm. In Dutch. In danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: 113 Zelfmoordpreventie
resources.what: Free, anonymous help by phone or chat, day and night, if you are thinking about suicide or worried about someone.
resources.how: Call 113 (or 0800-0113) from the Netherlands, or chat on the website. The website has a page in English.

resources.name: De Kindertelefoon
resources.what: For children and young people who want to talk about anything that is on their mind.
resources.how: Call 0800-0432 or chat, every day from 11am to 9pm. In Dutch.

resources.name: Kinderbijslag (child benefit)
resources.what: A regular payment towards the cost of raising your children.
resources.how: Register your baby's birth with your municipality. The SVB then sends you a letter within a few weeks, and you apply online in My SVB with DigiD or ask for a paper form. Register your baby with your health insurer within 4 months too.

resources.name: Kindgebonden budget
resources.what: An extra contribution towards the costs of children under 18, if you meet the conditions. With shared care, it goes to the parent who gets the kinderbijslag.
resources.how: If you qualify, you usually get a letter from the Dienst Toeslagen without having to apply. The full conditions are on toeslagen.nl.

resources.name: Free childhood vaccinations
resources.what: The vaccines in the national programme are free for children from birth to 18.
resources.how: Your child gets them at the consultatiebureau or the youth health service in your area.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: Women's Refuge crisis line
resources.what: Free information, advice and crisis help about family violence, any hour, from anywhere in New Zealand. Refuges run safe houses in every region.
resources.how: Call 0800 REFUGE. Do not let the person hurting you know you are thinking of leaving.

resources.name: 1737, Need to talk?
resources.what: Free call or text any hour to talk with a trained counsellor, or with a peer support worker, about feeling down, anxious or overwhelmed.
resources.how: Call or text 1737.

resources.name: PlunketLine
resources.what: Free parenting and child health advice from a registered nurse any hour, for children up to five. Free from mobiles too, and you do not need to be a Plunket client.
resources.how: Call any time. Ask for an interpreter if you need one. Breastfeeding and sleep video support can be booked through the line.

resources.name: Working for Families
resources.what: Payments to help with the cost of raising children 18 and under, based on family income. Best Start is part of it for babies.
resources.how: Check whether you qualify with the IRD calculator, then register in myIR or with the online form.

emergency.label: National emergency number, free from any network

resources.name: WARIF 24-hour helpline
resources.what: A free, confidential 24-hour line for women and girls who have faced rape, sexual violence or trafficking, reaching callers across Nigeria.
resources.how: Call 0800 921 0009. Shelter addresses are kept private; ask the helpline if you need a safe place.

resources.name: She Writes Woman helpline
resources.what: A free mental health line answered at any hour by trained counsellors. Callers do not need airtime.

resources.name: Lagos State DSVA helpline
resources.org: Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency
resources.what: For people in Lagos State facing domestic violence, sexual assault or abuse. The agency coordinates legal, medical, emergency and counselling help.
resources.how: Call 0800 0333 333 any hour, or dial *6820# to report.

resources.name: Cece Yara Child Helpline
resources.what: A free 24-hour helpline for children and parents, run by staff trained to talk with children. It focuses on child sexual abuse and gives free legal, medical and therapy help.

emergency.label: Ambulance and rescue. Police, dial 15. Fire, dial 16

resources.name: Helpline 1099
resources.what: A free government helpline for legal advice and help when your rights are violated. Most complaints it handles are about women's rights, and it can refer you to the right office.
resources.how: Dial 1099. You can also send a WhatsApp to 0333 9085709.

resources.name: Rozan Counseling Helpline
resources.what: Counselling by phone for emotional and mental health struggles, including violence against women and child sexual abuse.
resources.how: Call 0304 111 1741, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Benazir Nashonuma
resources.org: Ministry of Poverty Alleviation and Social Safety
resources.what: Cash every three months for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers and children under two in families on the Benazir Income Support Programme: PKR 2,000 for each mother and boy, and PKR 2,500 for each girl, with special nutritious food.
resources.how: It is for families already on the Benazir Income Support Programme. Mothers go to regular check-ups and keep their children's vaccines up to date.

emergency.label: Police. For fire, call 116; for an ambulance (SAMU), call 106

resources.name: Línea 100
resources.org: Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations (MIMP)
resources.what: Free, any hour, every day of the year, for anyone facing violence against women or family members, or who knows of a case. A team gives legal, psychological and social advice.
resources.how: Call 100 from a landline or mobile anywhere in Peru. Help is in Spanish, Quechua and Aymara. In danger right now, call 105.

resources.name: Línea 113, option 5
resources.what: Free, confidential help from psychologists, any hour, for an emotional crisis or when you feel at risk.
resources.how: Call 113 and choose option 5, or write on WhatsApp to 955 557 000. In Spanish.

resources.name: Juntos
resources.org: Ministry of Development and Social Inclusion (MIDIS)
resources.what: Money every two months for families in poverty with a pregnant woman, children or young people up to 19, as long as they keep up prenatal check-ups, child health checks and school.
resources.how: Families are chosen and signed up by MIDIS through its local staff.

emergency.label: Police, fire, medical and rescue

resources.name: NCMH Crisis Hotline
resources.what: The government's mental health crisis line, open any hour, for anyone in emotional distress or thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Dial 1553 toll-free from a landline. From a mobile, call 0919 057 1553 (Smart/TNT) or 0917 899 8727 (Globe/TM).

resources.name: Solo Parent ID
resources.org: City or Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office
resources.what: Under the Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act, a solo parent can get an ID that unlocks benefits such as leave, discounts and priority for some programs.
resources.how: Apply at your city or municipal social welfare office (or Solo Parent Office). The ID is renewed every year.

emergency.label: Any emergency. For an ambulance you can also call 999

resources.name: Niebieska Linia
resources.what: A free line, open around the clock, for people facing violence at home and for anyone who sees it happening.
resources.how: Call 800 120 002. In Polish.

resources.name: 116 123 emotional support line
resources.org: National helpline for people in emotional crisis
resources.what: A support line, open around the clock, for adults going through an emotional crisis.
resources.how: Call 116 123. In Polish.

resources.name: Centrum Wsparcia
resources.what: Free support, around the clock, for adults in a mental health crisis.
resources.how: Call 800 70 2222. In Polish.

resources.name: 116 111 helpline for children and young people
resources.org: Telefon Zaufania dla Dzieci i Młodzieży
resources.what: Free, anonymous support for children and teenagers.

resources.name: Rodzina 800+
resources.what: 800 zł a month for every child until they turn 18, whatever the family's income.
resources.how: Apply online to ZUS through PUE ZUS or the mZUS app, the Emp@tia portal, or your online bank. Apply within 3 months of your baby's birth to be paid from the day of birth.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance or the fire service, dial 995

resources.name: National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline (NAVH)
resources.org: Ministry of Social and Family Development
resources.what: A line open any hour to get help with, or report, family violence, abuse, neglect, sexual violence or sexual harassment. Victims, family, neighbours and professionals can all call.
resources.how: Call 1800-777-0000, or use the online report form. Airtime charges apply from a mobile.

resources.name: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS)
resources.what: Someone to talk to, any hour, if you are in crisis or having thoughts of suicide.
resources.how: Call 1767, or send a WhatsApp to CareText on 9151 1767. Both are open 24 hours. Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: ComCare
resources.org: Ministry of Social and Family Development
resources.what: Money help for families on a low income or in urgent need, from short-term help with living costs to help right away.
resources.how: Call the ComCare Hotline, open 7am to midnight every day, or visit a Social Service Office. For Singapore Citizens, and Permanent Residents living with a family member who is a citizen. Airtime charges apply from a mobile.

resources.name: Baby Bonus
resources.org: Ministry of Social and Family Development
resources.what: For each child who is a Singapore Citizen: a Cash Gift of $11,000 or more, paid in steps until age 6½, and a $5,000 grant into a Child Development Account, which the government also matches when you save. Parents must be married for the Cash Gift.
resources.how: Apply in the LifeSG app when you register the birth.

resources.name: Legal Aid Bureau
resources.what: Legal help with civil cases, including divorce, for people with limited means and a reasonable case. You can see a duty lawyer for advice.
resources.how: Register on the Legal Aid Bureau's applicant portal, then book an appointment before you go. Open weekdays, 8:30am to 5pm.

emergency.label: Police. From a cellphone, 112. Ambulance, 10177

resources.name: GBV Command Centre
resources.what: A 24-hour line staffed by social workers who give counselling and support to people facing gender-based violence, and can send a local social worker.
resources.how: Call toll-free, or dial *120*7867# from any cellphone to have them call you back.

resources.name: Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.org: South African Depression and Anxiety Group
resources.what: A toll-free crisis line, open any hour, for anyone thinking about suicide or worried about someone.
resources.how: Call toll-free from any network.

resources.name: Childline South Africa
resources.what: A free helpline any hour for children, and for adults worried about a child.
resources.how: Dial 116, free from all networks.

resources.name: Child Support Grant
resources.what: A monthly grant for the primary caregiver of a child under 18 in a low-income household.
resources.how: Apply free at your nearest SASSA office. Bring your ID and the child's birth certificate.

emergency.label: Any emergency, free from any phone, even with no credit or signal

resources.what: Free, confidential help any hour for women facing any form of violence, and for the people around them.
resources.how: Call 016, or send a WhatsApp message (no calls) to 600 000 016. The phone line works in 53 languages. You can also email 016-online@igualdad.gob.es.

resources.name: 024 suicide prevention line
resources.what: Free, confidential and open every hour of the year, for anyone with thoughts of suicide and for their family and friends.
resources.how: Call 024 from anywhere in Spain. There is also a chat run by the Red Cross and a sign language video service. If a life is in danger right now, call 112.

resources.name: ANAR helpline
resources.what: Free, confidential help for children and teenagers, any hour.
resources.how: Call 900 20 20 10 or open the chat on the website. In Spanish, with phone interpreting for other languages.

resources.name: Ingreso Mínimo Vital
resources.what: A monthly payment for people and families who do not have enough to cover the basics. Families on it with children also get a child supplement.
resources.how: Apply online at imv.seg-social.es and keep the reference code you are given. For information, call 020. In the Basque Country apply through Lanbide; in Navarra and Catalonia, through local offices.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: National Child Helpline 116
resources.org: C-Sema, with the Government of Tanzania
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, for children and for women and girls at risk of violence. Parents, family and neighbours can call to report a child in danger.
resources.how: Dial 116 from any phone.

resources.name: Afya Call Center
resources.what: Free health advice any hour from doctors and nurses, including mental health and sexual and reproductive health, and help finding a health facility near you.
resources.how: Dial 199.

emergency.label: Police. Fire, 990. Ambulance, 811

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline (800-SAVE)
resources.what: A line open any hour to get help with domestic or gender-based violence. It offers crisis help and counselling, and can arrange a place at the national shelter for women and their children.
resources.how: Dial 800-SAVE (800-7283). Normal call charges may apply.

resources.name: Lifeline
resources.what: Free, anonymous support any hour for anyone in emotional crisis or thinking about suicide.
resources.how: Call 800-5588 or 866-5433. Both are toll-free.

resources.name: Children's Authority hotline
resources.org: Children's Authority of Trinidad and Tobago
resources.what: The government agency that protects children. Call any hour to report a child you think is being abused or neglected.
resources.how: Dial 996 or 800-2014. Children who want to talk to someone can call Childline on 800-4321 or 131. Normal call charges may apply.

emergency.label: National emergency number. 112 works too

resources.name: Sauti 116
resources.org: Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development
resources.what: A free line, open day and night, to report abuse of a child or violence against a woman. Social workers and psychologists answer and pass cases on for help.
resources.how: Dial 116 from any phone. You can also text 116.

resources.name: MIFUMI domestic violence helpline
resources.what: A free line, open any hour, for women and children facing violence at home. Counsellors help you make a safety plan and can help with legal advice and emergency shelter.
resources.how: Call 0800 200 250. It is toll-free in Uganda.

resources.name: Mental Health Uganda toll-free line
resources.what: Free, confidential support with your mental health, on a weekday.
resources.how: Call 0800 21 21 21, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: National Domestic Abuse Helpline
resources.what: Free, confidential support any hour, every day of the year, from trained women advisers, in many languages. They can help with safety planning and finding a refuge.
resources.how: Call any time, or use the live chat on the helpline's website.

resources.name: Samaritans
resources.what: Someone to talk to, free, any time of day or night, from any phone. You do not have to be suicidal to call.

resources.name: PANDAS Foundation helpline
resources.what: Free support for parents struggling with their mental health in pregnancy and after birth, and for the people around them.
resources.how: Call Monday to Friday, 10am to 5pm, or book a call back on the website.

resources.name: National Breastfeeding Helpline
resources.org: Breastfeeding Network and Association of Breastfeeding Mothers
resources.what: Breastfeeding support any hour, every day, from trained volunteers who have breastfed. Help in Welsh and Polish is on the same number.
resources.how: Call any time. Calls cost the same as a call to a number starting 01 or 02.

resources.name: Gingerbread Single Parent Helpline
resources.what: Free advice for single parents in England and Wales on money, benefits, child maintenance, work, housing and separation.
resources.how: Call or use the webchat on the website. In Scotland, One Parent Families Scotland runs the Lone Parent Helpline on 0808 801 0323.

resources.name: Child Benefit
resources.what: A regular payment for each child you are responsible for. Only one person can claim for a child.
resources.how: Claim online or in the HMRC app from 48 hours after you register the birth. A claim can be backdated up to 3 months.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance

resources.name: Lifeline 933
resources.what: A free line for adults, open day and night, for gender-based violence, mental health worries and other hard times. Counsellors listen and refer you on for help.
resources.how: Call 933 for free. Texting and online counselling are offered too.

resources.name: Childline 116
resources.what: A free line for children, open day and night, in English and seven Zambian languages. It helps with abuse, neglect, child marriage, bullying and more.
resources.how: Dial 116 for free.

emergency.label: Police, fire and ambulance from an Econet phone. On NetOne, dial 114

resources.name: Musasa helpline
resources.what: A free line, open any hour, for women and girls facing violence at home or sexual violence. Musasa offers counselling, safe shelter, and help getting medical care quickly after rape.
resources.how: Call 08080074 from Econet or 08010074 from NetOne.

resources.name: Childline 116
resources.what: A free line for children up to 18, open day and night from any network. Adults can contact Childline to report a child being abused.
resources.how: Dial 116. You can also send a WhatsApp to +263 719 116 116.
